claims.rationale: The same subject has a distinct source-supported subsequent Zhou period of wider prevalence. Base /events/0 is Shang appearance, not Zhou prevalence. Existing description mentions Zhou but is not a dated event. Extend the existing capability rather than create a discovery for spread.
Identifier describes the sourced broader Zhou prevalence and does not imply a route.
dated_assertion expresses a broad prevalence change; the abstract names no recipient community or route and does not substantiate a specific transmission event.
The abstract explicitly uses Zhou 1027 to 221 BC for the increased prevalence. Bounds retain the whole source period; they are neither the onset nor a finding that spread was continuous throughout.
Subject proto-porcelain, action became more widespread, and Zhou time scope match the first abstract sentence. It asserts no mechanism, recipient, numerical uptake, or inferred causal relation.
China is the broad context of the first abstract sentence; it does not locate the change at any particular site or extend the scope beyond China.
The source and Abstract locator resolve to the original first sentence and the support statement preserves its wording and bounds.

UCL page confirms thesis title, Yin M, 2012, PhD and exact passage; saved excerpt matches the declared SHA-256 and contains the quotation in context. Source is abstract-level and duplicates an existing bibliographic source, not an independent source.

Proposal metadata, four claim paths, evidence and discovery hashes, direct-patch scope and duplicate-control descriptions agree with inspected patch and source. Execution ID and usage remain unavailable as disclosed.

causal_and_transmission_claims.requirement: Any future consequential causal or transmission link requires independent informative corroboration establishing direction, relationship and context; two source records of this same thesis are not independent evidence.
